application_type_full: Tree works: Trees in conservation areas/subject to TPOs
description: Pear tree in the middle of the garden.  It needs to be 'crowned'. .   2m all round leaving tree of 9m height above ground, to keep tree healthy.  This is what the tree surgeon told me it needed.  There is no TPO in place.
decision_conditions: Routine pruning is not required to maintain the health of a normal, mature tree. A healthy tree will sustain itself without cyclical crown reductions (crowning), and unnecessary cutting can in some cases create avoidable wounds that increase the risk of decay or structural weakness over time. Crown reduction is generally only recommended where there is a clear management need such as conflict with structures, limited space, or to address specific defects identified by a qualified arborist. Light pruning for clearance or form can be appropriate, but reductions should not be assumed to improve the underlying health of an otherwise sound tree.
